blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Roof Replacement Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking about a new roof in Southbank or Melbourne? We break down costs per square metre, material options, and factors that affect your quote.
body: Roof replacement is one of the biggest investments you'll make in your home. In Melbourne, the cost varies widely depending on the material, roof shape, and accessibility. For a standard single-storey home in Southbank, you're looking at anywhere from $10,000 to $25,000 for a full metal roof replacement. Tile roofs are usually more expensive due to extra labour and structural checks.

Colorbond steel roofs remain popular in Melbourne because they're durable, fire-resistant, and come in a range of colours. Expect to pay around $70 to $120 per square metre installed. Terracotta and concrete tiles can run from $80 to $150 per square metre. If you're in a heritage area like South Melbourne, you may need specific approvals and matching materials, which adds cost.

The condition of your roof deck also matters. If the underlying timbers are rotted or the insulation is water-damaged, that will push the price up. A reputable roofer will always inspect the deck before quoting. Makeit uses drone inspections to get a clear picture without scaffolding, which saves time and money.

Don't forget hidden costs: skip bins, scaffolding, and council permits can add $1,000 to $3,000. Some roof replacements require a building permit, especially if you're changing materials or adding skylights. In Melbourne's climate, you also need to consider insulation and ventilation upgrades to prevent condensation in winter.

When comparing quotes, look beyond the bottom line. A cheap quote might miss important steps like sarking installation, flashings, or warranty coverage. Makeit provides a line-by-line breakdown so you know exactly what's included. We also handle all compliance and provide a 7-year workmanship warranty.

If you're planning a roof replacement in 2026, book your inspection early. Melbourne's tradies are in high demand, especially in spring and summer. Get two or three quotes from local specialists like Makeit who know the council requirements in Southbank, South Melbourne and Docklands. A well-installed roof adds value and protects your home for decades.

blogPosts.title: Cladding Replacement for Strata Buildings: What Owners Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Is your strata building due for cladding replacement? Learn about new regulations, material costs, and how to coordinate with minimal disruption to residents.
body: After recent building code changes in Victoria, many strata buildings in Southbank and Docklands are assessing their cladding. Non-compliant aluminium composite panels (ACP) must be replaced with fire-safe materials. Owners corporations face significant costs but also an opportunity to upgrade the building's look and energy efficiency.

The cost of cladding replacement varies by building size and material. For a typical 10-storey building in Southbank, expect $500,000 to $2 million depending on the complexity. Permitted materials include non-combustible fibre cement, aluminium with a fire-retardant core, and natural stone. Each has different installation requirements and lifespan.

The process starts with a cladding audit and consent from the owners corporation. Then you'll need a fire engineer report and building permit. Makeit specialises in coordinating these steps for strata committees. We handle council liaison, scaffolding, and resident communication so owners aren't left in the dark.

One of the biggest challenges is minimising disruption. Residents need access to their balconies and windows, and common areas must stay safe. Our team uses phased scaffolding and weekend work where possible. We also provide a dedicated project manager who updates residents via the digital portal.

Timing is critical. The Victorian Building Authority requires all high-risk cladding to be rectified by 2026. If your building hasn't started yet, act now to avoid penalties or insurance issues. Makeit can fast-track the approval process using our pre-approved designs and established council relationships.

After replacement, your building will not only be safer but more attractive to buyers. Modern cladding can improve thermal performance, reduce noise, and lower maintenance costs. Plus, it's a chance to refresh the external colour scheme. Speak to Makeit about a free inspection and quote for your Southbank or Docklands strata.

blogPosts.title: Electrical Upgrades for Melbourne Homes: Solar, Batteries & EV Chargers
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of going solar or adding an EV charger? We cover costs, rebates, and what to expect from an electrical upgrade in Southbank and surrounds.
body: Melbourne homes are going electric. With rising power bills and generous rebates, many homeowners in Southbank are investing in solar panels, home batteries and electric vehicle chargers. An electrical upgrade typically starts with a switchboard assessment to ensure it can handle the extra load.

A standard solar installation (6.6kW system) costs between $4,000 and $7,000 after the federal STC rebate. Add a 10kWh battery and you're looking at $12,000 to $18,000. The Victorian Solar Homes rebate can knock off up to $1,400 on panels and $4,800 on batteries if you meet the income criteria. Makeit's electrical team handles the paperwork and installation.

EV charger installation is another fast-growing service. A Level 2 (7.2kW) charger costs $1,500 to $3,000 installed, plus the charger itself. Some newer homes already have the wiring in place. We recommend a dedicated circuit to avoid overloading. In a terrace house in Richmond or South Melbourne, we often need to run new conduit from the meter box.

Don't forget data cabling. More work-from-home setups require high-speed ethernet and reliable Wi-Fi. Running structured data cables during a renovation is much cheaper than retrofitting. Makeit installs Cat6 cabling, access points, and smart home systems that integrate with your lighting and security.

Safety is paramount. Old fuse boxes with ceramic fuses should be replaced with modern safety switches (RCDs). We also test and tag all new installations. In Melbourne's damp winters, outdoor wiring must be weatherproofed correctly. Our electricians are licensed and insured for all residential and commercial work.

Planning an electrical upgrade? Start with a free inspection from Makeit. We'll assess your current switchboard, check your solar potential, and give you a fixed-price quote. Rebates change regularly, so we advise you on the best timing. Book now and join the growing number of Southbank homes running on clean energy.

blogPosts.title: Plumbing Repairs for Strata: Fixing Leaks, Drains & Water Ingress
blogPosts.excerpt: Water leaks and drainage issues can cause big headaches for strata committees. Learn how to identify problems early and choose the right plumber.
body: In multi-unit buildings, plumbing problems can quickly become complex. A leak in an upper apartment can damage several floors below, leading to mould, structural issues and costly repairs. Owners corporations need a plumber who understands both residential units and common property systems.

Common issues in Southbank strata include blocked kitchen drains, corroded hot water pipes, and failed waterproofing in bathrooms. Some older buildings have galvanised steel pipes that rust internally, restricting flow. A CCTV drain inspection can pinpoint the exact block without digging up the courtyard.

Water ingress through external walls or basements is another frequent complaint. Often it's a combination of poor drainage, failed sealants and ground water pressure. Makeit's plumbing division works alongside our cladding team to seal cracks, install sump pumps and regrade landscaping to direct water away.

The cost of plumbing repairs in strata varies. A simple drain unblocking might be $250 to $500, while replacing a 10-storey building's hot water system could run $50,000 to $100,000. Having a plumbing maintenance plan can catch small issues before they become emergencies. Makeit offers annual inspections for strata committees.

When choosing a plumber for your strata, look for one with commercial liability insurance and experience in multi-level buildings. Makeit carries $20 million public liability cover and has worked on dozens of strata projects in Southbank, Docklands and Port Melbourne. We provide detailed reports and photos for insurance claims.

Don't wait for a major flood. Regular plumbing audits can save your owners corporation thousands. Makeit offers a free inspection for strata committees in Southbank and surrounds. We'll check common area plumbing, hot water systems and drainage. Keep your building dry and your residents happy.
